title: The Great Pyramid of Giza Is Completed for Pharaoh Khufu
description: Standing 481 feet tall for over 3,800 years, the Great Pyramid of Giza was built as Pharaoh Khufu’s tomb from an estimated 2.3 million stone blocks.
longFormSummary:
• Built for Pharaoh Khufu of Egypt’s Fourth Dynasty, construction is estimated to have run from roughly 2580 to 2560 BCE.
  • The Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for over 3,800 years, until England’s Lincoln Cathedral surpassed it around 1311 CE.
  • It is the only intact survivor among the ancient world’s Seven Wonders.
  • Built from an estimated 2.3 million limestone and granite blocks, some weighing as much as 80 tons.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Britannica and multiple Egyptology sources place the Great Pyramid’s completion at approximately 2560 BCE, with no exact date recorded.

title: Neolithic Builders Raise Stonehenge’s Sarsen Circle
description: Around 2500 BCE, Neolithic Britons hauled 25-ton sarsen stones roughly 20 miles to Salisbury Plain and raised them into the trilithons and circle known as Stonehenge.
longFormSummary:
• Around 2500 BCE, Stone Age builders erected Stonehenge’s sarsen stone circle and trilithons, widely regarded as the peak of Neolithic megalithic engineering in Britain.
  • The sarsens were transported roughly 20 miles from the Marlborough Downs using only muscle power and simple tools, before being dressed smooth on site.
  • Builders used mortise-and-tenon and tongue-and-groove joints — woodworking techniques translated into stone — to lock the five-ton lintels onto the uprights.
  • The sarsen circle followed an earlier earthwork enclosure built around 3000 BCE, part of a monument built and modified over some 1,500 years.
dateConfidenceReasoning: English Heritage and Britannica date the erection of Stonehenge’s sarsen circle and trilithons to approximately 2500 BCE.

title: Ptolemy II Completes the Lighthouse of Alexandria
description: The Pharos of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, was completed under Ptolemy II to guide ships into the city's Great Harbor. Commissioned by Ptolemy I and built by the architect Sostratus of Cnidus, the tower stood for over 1,600 years.
longFormSummary:
• Commissioned by Ptolemy I Soter after Alexander the Great founded Alexandria in 331 BCE.
  • Built by the architect Sostratus of Cnidus on the harbor island of Pharos, linked to the mainland by the Heptastadion mole.
  • Completed under Ptolemy II Philadelphus around 280 BCE, becoming one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
  • Guided ships into Alexandria's Great Harbor for over 1,600 years until earthquakes toppled it in the 14th century.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Ancient sources place completion under Ptolemy II around 280 BCE, per the World History Encyclopedia and Britannica; the exact year is not precisely recorded.

title: Qin Shi Huang Unifies China’s Border Walls Into the Great Wall
description: Around 220 BCE, China’s first emperor ordered the rival kingdoms’ old border walls linked into one defensive line, the earliest version of what became the Great Wall.
longFormSummary:
• Qin Shi Huang unified China in 221 BCE and ordered existing Warring States-era border walls joined into a single defensive system.
  • General Meng Tian directed the project, using soldiers, convicts, and commoners to extend the line roughly 10,000 li (about 5,000 km).
  • The Qin wall was built mostly of rammed earth; the stone-and-brick wall most visitors see today near Beijing is a later Ming dynasty rebuild.
  • An estimated 400,000 laborers are believed to have died during construction, with some reportedly buried within the wall itself.
dateConfidenceReasoning: History.com and the Qin dynasty's Wikipedia entry date Qin Shi Huang's order to join the northern border walls into one system to around 220 BCE, without a more precise date surviving.

title: Angkor Wat, the Largest Religious Monument on Earth, is Completed for Suryavarman II
description: Cambodia's Khmer king Suryavarman II built Angkor Wat as his state temple and eventual mausoleum, a 400-acre complex whose construction ran from around 1122 to 1150 CE.
longFormSummary:
• Khmer king Suryavarman II commissioned Angkor Wat as his personal state temple and mausoleum, dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu.
  • Construction ran from around 1122 CE and was largely complete by 1150 CE, the year of Suryavarman II's death, using an estimated 300,000 workers and 6,000 elephants over the project.
  • Covering roughly 162.6 hectares (400 acres) near Siem Reap, it remains the largest religious monument in the world by land area.
  • Unlike most Angkor temples oriented east, Angkor Wat faces west, a design choice linked to its funerary role.

dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia's Angkor Wat article states construction "commenced in 1122 CE and was completed in 1150 CE," a period-based estimate rather than a single confirmed day, consistent with other sources citing the reign of Suryavarman II (1113-1150).

title: Santa Maria della Salute Is Consecrated on Venice's Bed of a Million Piles
description: Venice's Baroque votive basilica, its foundations built on more than a million driven wooden piles in the lagoon mud, is consecrated by Patriarch Alvise Sagredo. The city still marks the day every November 21st as the Festa della Salute.
longFormSummary:
• Venice vowed the church in 1630 to give thanks for deliverance from a devastating plague outbreak.
  • Architect Baldassare Longhena's octagonal design rests on more than 1,000,000 oak and fir piles driven into the waterlogged lagoon floor.
  • Construction ran for over fifty years, outlasting Longhena himself, who died a year before completion.
  • Patriarch Alvise Sagredo consecrated the basilica on November 21, 1687, a date still celebrated annually as the Festa della Salute.
address: Basilica di Santa Maria della Salute, Punta della Dogana, Venice, Italy
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia and Venetian tourism histories date the consecration, by Patriarch Alvise Sagredo, to November 21, 1687 - still marked annually as the Festa della Salute.

title: Fenton, Murray and Wood Launches the Salamanca, the First Commercial Steam Locomotive
description: At the Round Foundry in Holbeck, Leeds, engineering firm Fenton, Murray and Wood built the Salamanca, the world's first commercially successful steam locomotive, which first ran publicly on 24 June 1812. Designed by Matthew Murray for John Blenkinsop's rack-and-pinion Middleton Railway, it hauled coal using a toothed rail system.
longFormSummary:
• Matthew Murray, a partner at the Round Foundry works of Fenton, Murray and Wood in Holbeck, Leeds, designed the Salamanca locomotive.
  • Salamanca first appeared in public on 24 June 1812, hauling coal on John Blenkinsop's rack railway, the Middleton Railway.
  • It was the first of four twin-cylinder locomotives built for the line and is recognised as the first commercially successful steam locomotive.
  • The Round Foundry, established in 1795, is regarded as the birthplace of British locomotive manufacturing.

title: Henraux Begins Quarrying Marble at Monte Altissimo
description: In 1821, landowner Marco Borrini and French businessman Jean-Baptiste Alexandre Henraux founded the Henraux marble company in Tuscany’s Apuan Alps. It still works the Monte Altissimo quarries first opened by Michelangelo in the 1500s and shown in Stone Men.
longFormSummary:
• Marco Borrini partnered with French businessman Jean-Baptiste Alexandre Henraux to found the Henraux quarrying company in 1821.
  • The company took over Monte Altissimo's marble deposits in the Apuan Alps, first identified for quarrying by Michelangelo around 1517.
  • Within a decade, Henraux expanded its holdings on the mountain from 11 to 132 quarries, employing hundreds of local quarrymen.
  • Today Henraux owns the entire mountain and still extracts marble from five active quarries, including the Henraux and Michele's Russia quarries featured in Stone Men.

title: Carr's Opens Its Carlisle Biscuit Works, Later Home to McVitie's
description: Jonathan Dodgson Carr founds a small bakery and biscuit factory in Carlisle, pioneering mass biscuit production. The site is still operating today as a McVitie's factory, the world's oldest continually-running biscuit works.
longFormSummary:
• Jonathan Dodgson Carr, a Quaker grocer's son, started a small bakery and biscuit factory in Carlisle in 1831.
  • Carr's became the first biscuit maker to receive a Royal Warrant, from Queen Victoria in 1841, and grew into Britain's largest baking business within 15 years.
  • The Caldewgate site was sold to United Biscuits in 1972 and rebranded as a McVitie's factory in the 1970s.
  • It remains the world's oldest continually-operating biscuit factory, now producing tens of millions of biscuits a day.

title: Great Indian Peninsula Railway Runs India's First Passenger Train
description: On April 16, 1853, the Great Indian Peninsula Railway ran the first passenger train in India and Asia, carrying about 400 guests roughly 34km from Bombay's Bori Bunder to Thane.
longFormSummary:
• Fourteen carriages carrying about 400 invited guests departed Bori Bunder station in Bombay behind three steam locomotives named Sahib, Sindh and Sultan.
  • The roughly 34km run to Thane took about an hour and 15 minutes, launching the first passenger rail service on the Indian subcontinent.
  • The Great Indian Peninsula Railway, formed under British colonial administration, had begun building the line in 1850 as part of a network meant to move troops, goods and administration across India.
  • Bori Bunder station was later rebuilt as Victoria Terminus in 1888, known today as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus.
address: Bori Bunder (now Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus), Mumbai, India
dateConfidenceReasoning: Confirmed by IRFCA's Indian Railways history FAQ and multiple independent sources, which date India's first passenger train from Bori Bunder to Thane to April 16, 1853.

title: Metropolitan Railway Opens the World's First Underground Line
description: The Metropolitan Railway opened between Paddington and Farringdon on January 10, 1863, the world's first underground railway and the ancestor of every metro system shown in Moving Millions Every Day.
longFormSummary:
• Built by cut-and-cover methods starting in 1860, the Metropolitan Railway opened its first section between Paddington and Farringdon Street on January 10, 1863.
  • It was the world's first underground passenger railway, with steam locomotives hauling gas-lit wooden carriages through the tunnels.
  • The line carried about 38,000 passengers on its opening day and 9.5 million in its first year, proving underground travel could work at city scale.
  • Its success set the template later followed by the metro systems in London, New York, Tokyo, Paris and elsewhere that the documentary credits with shaping the modern commuter city.
address: Paddington to Farringdon, London, United Kingdom
dateConfidenceReasoning: The London Transport Museum and Britannica both date the Metropolitan Railway's opening between Paddington and Farringdon to January 10, 1863.

title: City of Paris Opens Its Sewers to Public Tours During the 1867 World's Fair
description: During the 1867 Exposition Universelle, Paris opened Baron Haussmann's newly rebuilt sewer network to public tours for the first time, turning Eugène Belgrand's engineering into a civic showcase.
longFormSummary:
• Haussmann's renovation of Paris in the 1850s-60s included a wholesale rebuild of the city's sewer network, engineered by Eugène Belgrand.
  • For the 1867 World's Fair, officials raised the height of select galleries so visitors could walk through them.
  • The novelty tours drew fairgoers and dignitaries and proved popular enough to become a recurring public attraction.
  • What began as wagon and boat tours evolved into today's Paris Sewer Museum (Musée des Égouts) near the Pont de l'Alma.
dateConfidenceReasoning: The Paris sewer museum's own history page states tours "began in 1867, during the World's Fair" without naming an exact day, so the pin uses the Fair's opening date.

title: The Brooklyn Bridge Opens
description: New York's Brooklyn Bridge opened to the public, completing a 14-year construction effort that Emily Warren Roebling steered to completion after her husband was incapacitated by decompression sickness.
longFormSummary:
• Chief engineer John Roebling died of tetanus before construction began; his son Washington Roebling took over but was left disabled by caisson sickness while building the towers.
  • Washington's wife, Emily Warren Roebling, studied engineering and effectively ran day-to-day construction for over a decade on his behalf.
  • At its 1883 opening the bridge was the longest suspension bridge in the world, with President Chester A. Arthur attending the dedication and Emily Roebling given the first crossing.
address: Brooklyn Bridge, New York, NY, USA

title: Neuschwanstein Castle Opens to the Public
description: Bavaria's unfinished fairy-tale castle, built for King Ludwig II and left incomplete at his sudden death, opened to paying visitors for the first time.
longFormSummary:
• Ludwig II began planning the hilltop castle in 1868 after losing his political power, modelling its towers on the Wartburg and the operas of Richard Wagner.
  • Construction combined 19th-century steel framing with hand-carved stone and brick, and dragged on for years as Ludwig kept revising the design.
  • Ludwig died in June 1886 having lived in only a handful of finished rooms; the Bavarian state opened the half-built castle to the public within weeks to help recoup its enormous cost.
  • Neuschwanstein has never been fully completed - several planned halls were abandoned - yet it remains one of the most visited castles in the world.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "was opened to the public from 1 August 1886".

title: The Statue of Liberty Is Dedicated in New York Harbor

  • At completion it held records as the tallest iron structure and the largest copper repoussé sculpture ever built.
  • Shipped from France in 350 separate pieces, the statue was reassembled on what is now Liberty Island in New York Harbor.

title: The Washington Monument Opens to the Public
description: After decades of stalled funding and a visible change in stone partway up its shaft, the Washington Monument finally opened its doors to visitors in 1888.
longFormSummary:
• Construction began in 1848 but stalled for over 20 years for lack of funds and due to the Civil War, leaving a half-built stump for decades.
  • When work resumed in the 1880s, builders used marble from a different quarry, leaving the visible colour band still seen on the obelisk today.
  • The structural stonework topped out in December 1884, and the monument was formally dedicated in February 1885.
  • A steam elevator was then installed, and the monument opened to the public on October 9, 1888.
address: Washington Monument, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Gustave Eiffel’s Company Completes the Eiffel Tower
description: Gustave Eiffel’s engineering firm finished the Eiffel Tower in Paris after just over two years of construction, built as the entrance arch for the 1889 Exposition Universelle. The 300-metre iron lattice tower was the tallest man-made structure in the world at the time.

  • The tower served as the entrance arch for the 1889 Exposition Universelle (World’s Fair) in Paris.
  • At 300 metres, it became the tallest man-made structure in the world, a title it held for 41 years.

title: Orange County Opens the Frank R. Bowerman Landfill
description: In 1990, Orange County opened the Frank R. Bowerman Landfill in the hills above Irvine, California, which grew into the ninth-largest landfill in the United States.
longFormSummary:
• Orange County opened the site — originally called Bee Canyon Landfill — in 1990 to serve the county’s central waste disposal needs, later renaming it for environmental engineer Frank R. Bowerman.
  • It is the ninth-largest landfill in the United States and part of what’s informally called the "Million Ton Club" of the country’s biggest disposal sites.
  • The site now holds an estimated 31 million tons of waste in the western Santa Ana Mountains above Irvine.
  • It remains one of the busiest active landfills in the U.S., processing a share of the roughly 268 million tons of garbage generated nationally each year.

title: The Channel Tunnel Opens

longFormSummary:

  • Queen Elizabeth II and French President François Mitterrand presided over the opening ceremony on May 6, 1994.

title: How Frank Gehry's Guggenheim Bilbao Changed Architecture Forever
description: Frank Gehry's titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum Bilbao opened in October 1997, reviving a struggling industrial city and popularizing the aircraft-design software that made its curved form buildable.
longFormSummary:
• The Basque regional government funded the $100 million museum as part of a broader plan to revive Bilbao after its steel and shipbuilding industries collapsed.
  • Gehry's team used CATIA, 3D modelling software developed for fighter jets and Boeing aircraft, to translate the building's curved forms into roughly 33,000 buildable titanium panels.
  • Falling titanium prices after the Soviet Union's collapse, driven by decommissioned submarine hulls entering the market, made the unusual cladding choice affordable.
  • The museum opened on 18 October 1997 and drew 1.3 million visitors in its first year, more than triple initial projections, becoming a template for culture-led urban regeneration.

title: Jubilee Line Platforms Open at Westminster Underground
description: The deep-level Jubilee line platforms at Westminster Underground opened, completing London's £3.5bn Jubilee Line Extension after engineers dug a 30-metre station box beside the Thames without disturbing Big Ben's foundations.
longFormSummary:
• Westminster was the final station to open on the Jubilee Line Extension, built as an integrated structure beneath Hopkins Architects' Portcullis House.

  • The Circle and District line tracks above were lowered and temporarily suspended on a bridge structure so the deep box below could be dug using top-down construction.
  • Jubilee line tracks were stacked rather than laid side by side to minimise the station's footprint next to the Thames and the Palace of Westminster.

title: BHP Iron Ore Sets the World Record for Longest, Heaviest Freight Train

title: Volvo's Ghent Truck Plant Becomes the World's First CO2-Free Vehicle Factory

title: China's $1BN Skyscraper Mistake
description: The Shanghai World Financial Center opened in 2008 after developers were forced to redesign its circular summit opening into a trapezoid when the public read it as a Japanese flag.
longFormSummary:
• Architect William Pedersen of KPF originally designed a circular void at the top of the tower, referencing an ancient Chinese symbol for the sky.
  • After construction resumed following the 1997 Asian financial crisis, public backlash grew over the circle resembling the Japanese flag; the design was changed to a trapezoid in 2005.
  • Structural engineer Leslie Robertson reworked the frame to let the taller, wider revised tower still use foundations sized for the original design.
  • The tower opened in 2008, briefly the world's tallest building by roof height, before the Burj Khalifa surpassed it the following year.

title: Ciudad Real Central Airport Opens South of Madrid
description: A privately financed airport built to rival Madrid-Barajas opened near Ciudad Real in December 2008, before closing within four years as one of Spain's most notorious infrastructure failures.
longFormSummary:
• Built about 170km south of Madrid, the airport opened on 19 December 2008 as Spain's first privately financed airport, with a runway long enough for an Airbus A380.
  • It cost more than €1.1BN, but the high-speed rail station meant to connect it to Madrid was never built, leaving a footbridge that ends in an empty field.
  • Passenger numbers never came close to projections; the last scheduled flight departed in October 2011 and the airport formally closed in April 2012.
  • Its operating company went bankrupt in 2012, and after a rejected €10,000 bid in 2015 the site was eventually sold and reopened in 2019 as an aircraft maintenance and dismantling hub.
address: Ciudad Real Central Airport, Ciudad Real, Castilla-La Mancha, Spain
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Opened in 2008, the airport shut down just four years later."

title: China's Ministry of Commerce Cuts Rare Earth Export Quotas by 72%
description: China's Ministry of Commerce slashed its second-half 2010 rare earth export quotas by 72%, tightening its grip on the roughly 97% of global rare earth supply it mined at the time. • On July 9, 2010, China's Ministry of Commerce announced it would cut rare earth export quotas by 72% for the second half of the year, capping shipments at 7,976 metric tons versus 28,417 tons for the same period a year earlier.

title: Ryugyong Hotel's Exterior Finally Completed After 24 Years
description: Egyptian contractor Orascom finished cladding Pyongyang's pyramid-shaped Ryugyong Hotel in glass in July 2011, ending a stop-start construction saga that began in 1987 — though the 330-metre tower has never opened to a single guest.
longFormSummary:
• Construction began on the 330-metre, pyramid-shaped Ryugyong Hotel in August 1987, when North Korea set out to build the tallest hotel in the world.
  • Work froze completely in 1992 after North Korea’s economy collapsed following the fall of the Soviet Union, leaving a bare concrete shell for 16 years.
  • Egyptian firm Orascom Construction resumed work in 2008 and finished installing the glass exterior and telecom antennae by July 2011.
  • The interior was never fitted out, and decades on the 105-storey tower remains unopened, earning it the nickname “Hotel of Doom.”
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per en.wikipedia.org: "In July 2011, it was reported that the exterior work was complete."

title: Sinovel Installs China's First 5-Megawatt Offshore Wind Turbine at Donghai Bridge
description: Sinovel completed installation of the SL5000, China's first independently developed 5-megawatt offshore wind turbine, as a single demonstration unit at the Donghai Bridge wind farm near Shanghai. Two of China's largest crane vessels assembled the 150-meter-tall machine through the region's typhoon season.
longFormSummary:

title: Five Pacific islands lost to rising seas as climate change hits
description: Using time series aerial and satellite imagery from 1947 to 2014 of 33 islands, along with historical insight from local knowledge, we have identified five vegetated reef islands that have vanished over this time period and a further six islands experiencing severe shoreline recession.
longFormSummary:
• A 2016 study published in Environmental Research Letters examined how sea-level rise and wave exposure interact to erode low-lying reef islands in the Solomon Islands, a region with some of the highest rates of sea-level rise in the world.
  • Researchers analyzed aerial photographs from 1947-1962 and satellite imagery from 2002-2014 across 33 islands, combined with wave-energy hindcast data and radiocarbon dating of trees.
  • Five vegetated reef islands vanished entirely and six more lost over 20% of their area during the study period.
  • Erosion accelerated sharply on the more wave-exposed Isabel islands, where shoreline recession rates rose from about 0.1% annually (1947-1962) to 1.9% annually (2002-2014), compared with minimal change in the more sheltered Roviana region, where wave energy was twenty times lower.
  • At two Isabel sites, erosion destroyed villages that had existed since at least 1935, forcing community relocations.
  • The study concludes that sea-level rise and high wave exposure interact synergistically, meaning local wave conditions can dramatically amplify a coastline's vulnerability to climate-driven erosion.

title: AMD reveals details for Kaveri APU

title: World's Largest Solar Array Set to Crank Out 290 Megawatts of Sunshine Power
description: The plant comprises more than five million solar panels that span the equivalent of two Central Parks in the desert between Yuma and Phoenix.   • The plant includes extra panels with smart controls that can be brought online to compensate for output lost when clouds pass overhead.
  • The achievement is notable in context: just four years earlier, the largest solar facility in the US generated only 20 megawatts.

title: Retina iMacs and Apple Displays Within Reach as New DisplayPort 1.3 Spec Finalized
description: With Dell having announced its upcoming 5120 x 2880 "5K" display that would be the equivalent of a Retina 27-inch iMac or Apple Thunderbolt...
longFormSummary:
• The Video Electronics Standards Association finalized the DisplayPort 1.3 specification on September 15, 2014, increasing usable bandwidth by 50% to roughly 25.92 Gbps of video data (32.4 Gbps total).
  • That extra bandwidth is enough to drive a single 5120x2880 "5K" display without compression over one cable, or to run dual 4K displays off a single connection using DisplayPort's Multi-Stream feature — both of which the previous DisplayPort 1.2a standard couldn't do without compression.

title: California Law Now Requires All Smartphones to Have Built-In Kill Switches By July 2015
description: A California bill requiring all smartphones sold in the state to have antitheft technology installed was today signed into law by California governor...
longFormSummary:
• California's SB-962 "kill switch" bill, signed into law by Governor Jerry Brown on August 25, 2014, requires all smartphones sold in the state to include built-in antitheft technology, effective July 2015.
  • The technology must be able to render a lost or stolen phone inoperable to unauthorized users, survive a hard reset or OS downgrade, and prevent a stolen phone from being reactivated on a wireless network without the original owner's authorization, while remaining reversible for the legitimate owner and enabled during initial device setup.
  • Apple's iPhones already satisfy the requirement through Activation Lock, tied to iCloud accounts, while other manufacturers like Samsung and Microsoft would need to build comparable features.
  • The law sits in a broader context of anti-theft efforts aimed at reducing smartphone theft in major cities: Minnesota had passed a similar law, several manufacturers had voluntarily committed to kill-switch features by July 2015, and a federal Smartphone Theft Prevention Act was under consideration that could extend the requirement nationwide.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Date has passed, but macrumors.com does not confirm it happened then; unverified.

title: Torre Reforma Becomes Mexico City's Tallest Building
description: A 57-storey concrete-and-glass tower on Paseo de la Reforma, engineered to ride out centuries of predicted earthquakes, topped out as Mexico City's tallest building.
longFormSummary:
• Architect Benjamín Romano's triangular tower pairs a glazed main facade with two chamfered concrete walls that echo pre-Hispanic and colonial Mexican masonry.
  • Engineers at Arup modelled roughly 2,500 years of regional seismic activity to size the tower's concrete shear walls and coupling beams for earthquake resistance.
  • A historic 1929 house at the base of the site was underpinned and slid out of the way on steel runners during construction, then moved back into place as part of the lobby.
  • At 246 metres and 57 storeys, it overtook Torre BBVA Bancomer and Torre Mayor to become the city's tallest building upon completion.
address: Torre Reforma, Avenida Paseo de la Reforma 483, Cuauhtémoc, Mexico City, Mexico
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Upon completion in 2016 it became the tallest skyscraper in Mexico City".

title: City of Paris Inaugurates La Canopée at Les Halles
description: Paris unveiled La Canopée, a sweeping glass-and-steel roof capping the decade-long, roughly 800 million euro renovation of the Forum des Halles shopping and transit hub. Mayor Anne Hidalgo led the inauguration of the structure designed by architects Patrick Berger and Jacques Anziutti.
longFormSummary:
• The renovation replaced the 1970s Forum des Halles complex above Paris's busiest metro/RER hub.
  • Architects Patrick Berger and Jacques Anziutti designed La Canopée, a 14-meter-high glass and steel canopy.

title: Fifty-six percent of California voters approved Proposition 64 Legalizing Marijuana
description: Proposition 64, The Adult Use Marijuana Act, permits adults over 21 years of age who are not participating in the state’s medical cannabis program to legally grow (up to six plants, including all of the harvest from those plants) and to possess personal use quantities of cannabis (up to one ounce of flower and/or up to eight grams of concentrates) while also licensing commercial cannabis production and retail sales
longFormSummary:
• Proposition 64, California's Adult Use Marijuana Act, took effect November 9, 2016 and legalized cannabis for adults 21 and older.
  • Adults may possess up to one ounce of flower and/or eight grams of concentrate, cultivate up to six plants at home (keeping the full harvest from those plants), and gift up to one ounce to another adult without payment.
  • Violations outside those limits carry penalties: possessing more than 28.5 grams of flower or 8 grams of concentrate, growing more than six plants, or selling/delivering cannabis without a license are each misdemeanors carrying up to six months in jail and a $500 fine, while illegally manufacturing concentrates using volatile chemicals is a felony punishable by three to seven years in prison and up to a $50,000 fine.
  • For minors under 18, most possession and distribution violations are treated as infractions requiring drug counseling and/or community service rather than jail time, though violations on school grounds carry enhanced penalties.
  • The law also created a path for people to petition to have past marijuana convictions expunged, and left California's existing medical marijuana program in place alongside the new adult-use rules.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild lands top spot on IGN's 10 Best Legend of Zelda Games of All Time
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild reinvented a 30-year-old series in a way we rarely see. After Skyward Sword offered a slightly more linear, story-driven campaign than most fans were used to, Breath of the Wild readjusted dramatically in the opposite direction. Suddenly you could go anywhere and climb anything in any order you wanted, and goodness gracious was there a whole lot to choose from.

There are plenty of fair criticisms to throw at Breath of the Wild, with common ones being its lack of traditional Zelda dungeons and items. But what’s truly impressive is how much it maintained the heart of a Zelda game even as it altered nearly every system around it. To a certain extent, Zelda has always been about exploration and choice, and Breath of the Wild simply leaned into and enabled those aspects of itself above all else, now making the world a place that would react to those choices as well. There’s just so much to see, so many people to meet and secrets to find hidden throughout this long-since devastated version of Hyrule.

title: UK's Newest Fusion Reactor Just Generated Its First Plasma
description: The United Kingdom switched on its newest fusion reactor last week, and the ST40 has already hit a milestone -- plasma within its core. The reactor, created by Tokamak Energy, should heat plasma to 100 million degrees Celsius (or 180 million degrees Fahrenheit)

• In late April 2017, UK-based Tokamak Energy achieved "first plasma" in its ST40 fusion reactor at its facility in Oxfordshire, England, a milestone in the privately funded company's five-stage development plan (ST40 representing stage three).
  • The reactor is designed to eventually heat plasma to 100 million degrees Celsius (about 180 million degrees Fahrenheit) by 2018 — roughly seven times hotter than the core of the Sun — the temperature needed to fuse hydrogen into helium and release usable clean energy.
  • CEO David Kingham said the achievement showed that "fusion temperatures - 100 million degrees - are possible in compact, cost-effective reactors"; the company's stated goal is commercial-scale fusion power by 2030.
  • The milestone came amid other fusion advances worldwide, including MIT setting a plasma pressure record in October 2016, South Korea sustaining plasma near 300 million degrees for 70 seconds in December 2016, and Germany's Wendelstein 7-X stellarator successfully controlling plasma.
  • Significant cost, investment, and engineering hurdles remain before commercial fusion is realistic.

title: A New Doubly Charmed Particle Has Just Been Discovered in CERN
description: For many years, physicists have been aware of the existence of this doubly charmed particle because of current physical theories. However, nobody has been successful in observing the particle and it is only now that the baryon with two heavy quarks has been distinctively detected. Known as Ξcc++(Xicc++), this new particle is almost four times heavier than a proton.
longFormSummary:
• On July 7, 2017, the LHCb (Large Hadron Collider beauty) collaboration at CERN announced the discovery of a new particle designated Xi_cc++ (Ξcc++), made up of two charm quarks and one up quark.
  • It is the first confirmed observation of a baryon containing two heavy quarks — all previously known baryons contained at most one — and at roughly 3,621 MeV it is nearly four times heavier than a proton.
  • Physicists had theoretically predicted such doubly-charmed particles for years based on the Standard Model but had never directly observed one until this measurement.
  • LHCb physicist Giovanni Passaleva said the particle "will provide a unique tool to further probe quantum chromodynamics," the theory of the strong nuclear force that binds quarks together, and researchers expect it to help refine predictions of how quarks interact.
  • The team anticipates finding related particles in the same family, including baryons containing two beauty quarks or combinations of beauty and charm quarks, and plans to continue searching for them.

title: Hidroituango Dam Crisis Forces Mass Evacuation in Colombia
description: A blocked diversion tunnel at Colombia's roughly $4 billion Hidroituango hydroelectric project triggered flooding and landslides that forced thousands of people downstream to evacuate.

title: Key Takeaways of 2018 MacBook Pro vs. 2017 MacBook Pro
description:
2018 MacBook Pros feature eighth-generation Intel Core processors. Apple says the 15-inch model is up to 70 percent faster, and the 13-inch model is up to two times faster, than the equivalent 2017 models with seventh-generation Intel Core processors in benchmarks.
15-inch models can now be maxed out with a 2.9GHz six-core Core i9 processor, while the previous generation topped out at a 3.1GHz quad-core Core i7. Quad-core 13-inch models with the Touch Bar are now available, up to 2.7GHz, while 2017 models were dual-core up to 3.5GHz.
longFormSummary:
• This MacRumors article breaks down what changed when Apple refreshed the 13-inch and 15-inch MacBook Pro with Touch Bar on July 12, 2018.
  • The headline upgrade is 8th-generation Intel Core processors, which Apple said made the 15-inch model up to 70 percent faster and the 13-inch model up to twice as fast as the 2017 versions; the 15-inch can now be configured with a 2.9GHz six-core Core i9 (up from a quad-core Core i7 ceiling), and the 13-inch gained quad-core options up to 2.7GHz.
  • Other upgrades include RAM up to 32GB DDR4 on the 15-inch (versus 16GB LPDDR3 previously), doubled maximum storage (2TB on 13-inch, 4TB on 15-inch), a new Apple T2 security chip adding always-listening "Hey Siri" support, True Tone display technology across the line, Bluetooth 5.0, and a quieter third-generation butterfly keyboard.
  • Design, port layout (four Thunderbolt 3 ports), display resolutions, battery life rating, weight, and starting prices ($1,799 for 13-inch, $2,399 for 15-inch) all stayed the same.
  • The article notes it remained unclear whether the revised keyboard would resolve the reliability problems that had dogged earlier butterfly-switch keyboards.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per macrumors.com: "…dels, now availa … with any new product launch, there is a wealth of information to sift through, so…"

title: NASA's Groundbreaking Mission to 'Touch' the Sun Will Launch in 2018
description: NASA's Parker Solar Probe will be the first spacecraft to fly directly into the atmosphere of the Sun and explore its brutally hot corona.
longFormSummary:
• This article covers NASA's renaming of its Solar Probe Plus mission to the Parker Solar Probe, honoring astrophysicist Dr. Eugene Parker, who in 1958 published the foundational research establishing the theoretical basis for solar wind.
  • The spacecraft, targeted to launch in a window opening around July 31, 2018, will be the first mission to fly directly into the Sun's outer atmosphere, coming within about 4 million miles of the solar surface across 24 planned orbits through the corona.
  • To survive, it is shielded by a 4.5-inch-thick carbon-composite heat shield built to withstand extreme temperature swings and intense radiation.
  • The mission aims to resolve long-standing questions about why the corona is dramatically hotter than the Sun's surface and to study solar wind, flares, and coronal mass ejections.
  • This research aims to improve space-weather forecasting, with practical stakes for satellite communications, aviation safety, astronaut protection, and power infrastructure on Earth.

title: American Copper Buildings' Skybridge Completes in Manhattan
description: Developer JDS Development Group and architects SHoP completed the American Copper Buildings on Manhattan's East River in 2018, two leaning towers joined by a three-storey glass skybridge.
longFormSummary:
• Zoning split the site's buildable land into two separate lots around protected parkland and a school, so SHoP bent two towers toward each other and joined them with a bridge instead of building on one plot.
  • Installed from January 2016, the bridge spans floors 27-29 and holds a 75-foot lap pool and lounge; it was the first skybridge built in New York City in decades.
  • Because the towers lean in opposite directions and each floor shifts slightly as it nears the crossing, engineers had to design the bridge as a folding, non-orthogonal parallelogram.
  • The west tower opened in 2017 and the east tower, with the completed skybridge, followed in 2018.

title: Consorzio Venezia Nuova Installs the Last of MOSE's 78 Flood Gates
description: The consortium building Venice's MOSE flood-defence system put the last of its 78 mobile barrier gates into place across the lagoon's three inlets, completing two decades of construction. Heavy-lift specialist Fagioli spent years floating and positioning the multi-tonne steel gates before the system was tested for the first time in 2020.
longFormSummary:
• The last of MOSE's 78 mobile flood gates was put in place on 30 January 2019, ending the installation that began at Venice's three lagoon inlets in 2003
  • The 78 gates sit in four rows on the seabed, 21 and 20 at the Lido inlet, 19 at Malamocco and 18 at Chioggia, and are raised with compressed air to seal the lagoon off from the Adriatic during acqua alta
  • The Consorzio Venezia Nuova built the system for the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport's Venice Water Authority
  • Heavy-lift company Fagioli laid the barriers. It was engaged in 2012 for the Lido inlet, then built a taller 800-ton gantry crane to lower the 58 gates of the deeper Malamocco and Chioggia inlets onto their hinges, up to 14 m underwater
  • The gates are steel boxes 20 m wide and 18.5 to 29.5 m long, weighing from about 210 t at Lido to over 400 t at Malamocco and Chioggia
  • Placing the last gate did not finish the system: four gates were first raised in October 2013, the first full test of all 78 came on 10 July 2020, and MOSE first held back a real high tide on 3 October 2020. Wikipedia still listed the project as unfinished in November 2025
  • Construction cost is put at about €5.5 billion, €1.3 billion over the first projections, and the project was hit by 2014 corruption arrests that included Venice's mayor
  • Each inlet has two spare gates so that gates can be lifted out for maintenance, which Fagioli does with its gantry launching system
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia's MOSE article states the last of the 78 gates was put in place on 30 January 2019.

title: Nord Stream 2 Pipeline Finishes Construction
description: The $11BN Nord Stream 2 gas pipeline finished construction across the Baltic Sea, though it never entered commercial service and was later damaged by underwater explosions.
longFormSummary:
• The twin-line, 1,200km pipeline runs from Russia to Germany, built to roughly double Nord Stream's original capacity.
  • Construction used the world's largest pipe-laying vessel and finished in September 2021 after delays from US sanctions.
  • Germany suspended the certification process in February 2022 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, so it never carried gas commercially.
  • Explosions in September 2022 ruptured three of the pipeline's four lines, effectively ending the project.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Nord Stream 2 AG, which is 100% controlled by Gazprom, announced the completion of pipe laying for the second branch".

title: Le Commandant Charcot Becomes First LNG-Powered Ship to Reach the North Pole
description: Ponant's hybrid-electric icebreaker Le Commandant Charcot reached the Geographic North Pole on 6 September 2021, the first French vessel and the first LNG-propelled ship ever to do so.
longFormSummary:
• Le Commandant Charcot, built by VARD (hull at Vard Tulcea, Romania; outfitting at Vard Søviknes, Norway) and delivered to Compagnie du Ponant on 29 July 2021, is the world's first hybrid-electric, LNG-powered polar exploration icebreaker.
  • On 6 September 2021 the ship reached the Geographic North Pole after sailing from Svalbard, becoming the first French ship and the first LNG-powered ship in history to arrive there.
  • The 150m PC2-class vessel carries a Polar Class 2 hull, LNG-battery hybrid propulsion, and onboard systems that generate its own electricity and drinking water for full autonomy in the Arctic and Antarctic.
  • The milestone showcased engineering meant to cut the environmental footprint of polar cruising, six years and hundreds of engineers across Europe having gone into the ship's construction.
dateConfidenceReasoning: Confirmed by Cruise Industry News and Seatrade Cruise, which both report Le Commandant Charcot reached the Geographic North Pole on 6 September 2021.

title: Horizon Forbidden West Review  - IGN
description: Successful sequels build on their predecessors in multiple ways – think Mass Effect 2, Assassin's Creed 2, and Uncharted 2. They all improve what came before them by conjuring up exciting new gameplay mechanics, developing characters through engaging stories, and switching up mission design to offer variety. In other words, they take a solid base and combine with new elements to create more advanced bonds, much like an alloy… or in this case, an Aloy. Horizon Forbidden West does this with aplomb, building on the already impressive foundations of 2017’s Horizon Zero Dawn to tell a thrilling story full of familiar explosive combat against elaborate robotic foes and blockbuster action sequences, but also adding Witcher-like settlements to the map and filling it out with great side quests. There’s a genuine sense of exploration and loads of completely involving lore behind it all to uncover. The result is a fantastic open-world action-adventure that, despite falling into a couple of its old habits, emphatically delivers on the promises made five years ago.

title: New Ceramic Coating Could Make Hypersonic Air Travel a Reality
description: The new coating is 12 times more effective than current ceramics. Dennis Muilenburg, CEO of Boeing has said that hypersonic passenger jets could be in the air within the next ten years. These aircraft would cut travel times by up to 700 percent. This would mean a flight from Shanghai to New York would be reduced from 15 hours to just two.
longFormSummary:
• A team of Chinese and British scientists -- from the University of Manchester, the Royce Institute, and China's Central South University -- developed a new carbide-based ceramic coating using a manufacturing process called reactive melt infiltration, reinforcing zirconium carbide with a carbon-carbon composite.
  • The resulting coating is about 12 times more resistant to oxidation and degradation than current ceramics, which matters because aircraft flying at Mach 5 generate surface temperatures between roughly 3,600 and 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.
  • The article ties the research to industry momentum around hypersonic passenger travel: then-Boeing CEO Dennis Muilenburg predicted such jets could become reality within the next decade or two and cut travel times by up to 700 percent, turning a 15-hour Shanghai-to-New York flight into roughly two hours, while Boom Supersonic's CEO Blake Scholl noted five airlines had placed orders following the Paris Airshow.
  • Lockheed Martin and DARPA are also mentioned as pursuing hypersonic vehicle development.
  • The article is careful to note that commercial viability remains uncertain given the very high operating costs involved, and that the coating's more immediate applications are for spacecraft re-entry as well as potential future civilian hypersonic aircraft.

title: Elden Ring Review  - IGN
description: In the 87 hours that it took me to beat Elden Ring, I was put through an absolute wringer of emotion: Anger as I was beaten down by its toughest challenges, exhilaration when I finally overcame them, and a fair amount of sorrow for the mountains of exp I lost along the way to some of the toughest boss encounters FromSoftware has ever conceived. But more than anything else I was in near-constant awe – from the many absolutely jaw-dropping vistas, the sheer scope of an absolutely enormous world, the frequently harrowing enemies, and the way in which Elden Ring nearly always rewarded my curiosity with either an interesting encounter, a valuable reward, or something even greater. FromSoftware takes the ball that The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild got rolling and runs with it, creating a fascinating and dense open world about freedom and exploration above all else, while also somehow managing to seamlessly weave a full-on Dark Souls game into the middle of it. It shouldn’t be a surprise to anyone that Elden Ring ended up as one of the most unforgettable gaming experiences I’ve ever had.

title: Kirby and the Forgotten Land Review - IGN

title: The Quarry Review - IGN
description:
Like many of developer Supermassive’s previous games, The Quarry is clearly made both by and for people who love horror movies. From the start, it slowly builds tension and atmosphere, getting you invested by constantly asking you to make small decisions that will guide its teenage cast of potential murder victims. By the time the blood started flying, every choice felt like one more step in a rolling disaster, and that made it nearly impossible to put down. When I went back to replay it again, however, it was impossible to ignore just how non-interactive much of The Quarry actually is. As a spiritual sequel to Until Dawn, it's a better movie, but a worse game.

You follow the story of nine camp counselors who get stuck in the woods for one more night at the end of the summer, with nothing to do but throw one last party before they go back to their lives. There's something stalking them from the treeline (because of course there is) and your choices determine which, if any, of the counselors will be able to survive the night. This setup layers three fairly textbook horror plots on top of each other as you progress, but you can tell that Supermassive Games had a lot of fun figuring out how to connect them together. When you play, you may think you're in one type of horror movie, but you're often in another.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge Review - IGN
description:
Growing up as a child of the 90s, whenever I stepped into an arcade, I’d always do a walk around to see what they had before putting my quarters into any machines. This usually didn’t last very long because as soon as I saw a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles cabinet, I’d shout to my friends “They got Turtles!” and we’d rush on over.

It’s abundantly clear that the developers at Tribute Games share a similar love for the 90s TMNT beat-em-ups. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder’s Revenge is nothing but unwaveringly reverent to the classic 1989 Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Arcade game, and more prominently, 1991’s Turtles in Time. Best of all, it transforms the arcadey quarter-munching design of combat into something much more skill forward while still maintaining the same button mashy appeal. Put simply, Shredder’s Revenge is a prime example of how to breathe new life into a classic arcade beat-em-up.

title: As Dusk Falls Review - IGN

And it’s all about the story, since this is a choose-your-own-adventure-style graphic novel that cleverly pulls ideas from games like Telltale’s The Walking Dead series and 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim. Each member of this voice-acting cast of unique and interesting characters has their own, often conflicting emotional stakes that accelerate the story in seemingly hundreds of logical and intelligently connected directions. Through the powerful and often far-reaching consequences of your own actions, this small town is gradually unveiled as a powder keg full of secrets, vices, and familial bonds that run far deeper than any outsider is initially led to expect.

title: Stray Review - IGN
description:
A delightful cat-based platforming adventure in a cyberpunk world worth exploring.

Silent protagonists are nothing new in video games, but Stray certainly pushes that concept to an interesting place. Part platformer, part traditional adventure game, this cyberpunk world full of neon-soaked robots transforms into a giant jungle gym from your perspective, which is just one foot off the ground. The concept of putting you in the paws of an average cat may be a silly one on the surface, but Stray uses that furry vehicle to tell a genuinely compelling story with some entertaining action along the way. Not all of its ideas land on their feet, but it was impossible to shake the fuzzy feeling it gave me right from the adorable opening minutes.

title: China rolls out a further 1 trillion yuan in economic stimulus ($146 billion dollars)

title: Splatoon 3 Review: Single-Player  - IGN
description: Historically, Splatoon’s single-player campaigns have focused on acclimating you to the waters of its much more frantic and churning multiplayer battle modes. Splatoon 3’s campaign — dubbed The Return of the Mammalians — starts in territory so familiar that I was initially worried I was about to spend the next several hours slogging through tutorials on fundamentals I’d learned two games ago. Thankfully, the rug was quickly pulled out from under me, leading to a brand-new take on the series’ hub world design mixed with some of the best ideas of Splatoon 2’s Octo Expansion. Splatoon 3 boldly let me decide on whether or not to blaze my own path toward any of its 70 bite-sized, inventive missions, and choose where to go next when exploring its fuzzy ooze-filled world. A lot of the enemies I found there were unchanged from previous Splatoons, but I had a great time navigating the large variety of objectives all the way to the campaign’s explosively satisfying finale.

title: Gatwick Completes Main Runway Resurfacing
description: Gatwick Airport finished an overnight resurfacing of its main runway's busiest sections in September 2022, using a leaner method that cut the job to half the usual time and material.
longFormSummary:
• Gatwick's main runway hadn't been resurfaced since 2012, but a full traditional repaving was judged wasteful since much of it still had years of life left.
  • Crews instead resurfaced only the most heavily trafficked touchdown and taxi-off sections, working in narrow overnight windows between flights.
  • The approach used about 40,000 tonnes of asphalt versus the roughly 140,000 tonnes a full repave would need, cutting cost and carbon significantly.
  • The project wrapped up in September 2022, in around six months versus the year a conventional resurfacing would typically take.

title: A Plague Tale: Requiem Review - IGN
description: Like a sugar-crazed child working their way to the bottom of a Halloween bag full of treats, A Plague Tale: Requiem is confident that the things which made the first game great will be even more delectable in ludicrous quantities. You enjoyed a gruesome and harrowing journey that tested the limits of your emotional resilience? Great, let’s increase your personal suffering by 200%! This follow-up to one of my favorite action-adventure games of the previous console generation turns the dials up to 11 in practically every way, and overwhelmingly benefits from those escalations despite sometimes being a bit heavy on the nihilism. With improved stealth action mechanics, a fantastic (and deeply depressing) story, and graphics that had me gawking, A Plague Tale: Requiem is an impressive glow up that’s easily worth the immense horrors it subjected me to.

title: Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope Review - IGN
description:
When a game hits on a good idea, some developers are content to play it safe for the sequel, making a few refinements but largely stick to what worked the first time. That totally makes sense. But Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope is not that kind of sequel; even though Mario + Rabbids: Kingdom Battle surprised us all with its smart XCOM-style tactics in Nintendo clothing, this followup maintains its best ideas but reinvents itself to the point where it immediately feels very different. It’s bigger and better in nearly every way, with a more freeform and customizable take on combat and an almost completely rethought overworld that’s much less linear and absolutely packed with puzzles. The story’s all over the place and the Switch can’t always handle everything smoothly, but it’s a fantastic game that can be played as either an enjoyable cakewalk or a deep, demanding tactical challenge, all while maintaining its zany sense of humor.

Picking back up in the post-Rabbid invasion Mushroom Kingdom, things immediately get even weirder when a giant manta ray from space arrives to cause trouble. The story is actually one of Sparks of Hope’s few missteps: the original’s trans-dimensional blending of Mario characters and goofball Rabbids is completely absurd, but it kind of makes sense in its own way. This time, though, the completely unrelated enemy spreads what’s effectively Ganon’s corrupt ooze with eyeballs from Breath of the Wild everywhere, and most but not all of her minions are also Rabbids for some reason? Also we have a spaceship for traveling between literal worlds? It makes Kingdom Battle look grounded in reality by comparison, which is something I never thought I’d say about that game. I wasn’t expecting deep lore or anything, but it’s kind of a mess. It does consistently have some pretty good jokes, though, so at least I was chuckling as I was scratching my head.

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 review
description:
Modern Warfare 2's greatest strength is that it doesn't have a gimmick, because it doesn't need one.All Modern Warfare 2 needs to be is a great shooter, and it delivers. This is the Cal

Modern Warfare 2's greatest strength is that it doesn't have a gimmick, because it doesn't need one.

All Modern Warfare 2 needs to be is a great shooter, and it delivers. This is the Call of Duty experience, deconstructed, reconsidered, and obsessively optimized over 15 uninterrupted years of iteration. I know when I'm playing a Black Ops game because it has offbeat arcade modes and the latest iteration of Nuketown. I know I'm playing a Modern Warfare game because the shooting is so finely tuned that I want to take my Gunsmith build out to dinner. Infinity Ward has officially mastered the instant gratification of aiming down sights and deleting targets.

That goes a long way, though some of Modern Warfare 2's biggest swings, such as revamped progression and a genre-bending campaign, are less elegant. It also suffers from an obtuse UI, fits of crashes, weird bugs, and the unexplained absence of basic features like stat tracking. But altogether, it's a good year for Call of Duty.

title: Marvel's Midnight Suns Review - IGN
description: One of my favorite things about watching superheroes duke it out is when someone gets smacked so hard they fly backwards and crash through solid walls, explode tanker trucks, or slam into their friends. It’s an awesome demonstration of just how strong these godlike characters are supposed to be, and it’s always a disappointment when a superhero game doesn’t quite capture that feeling. With Marvel’s Midnight Suns, however, Firaxis has built a deep and innovative turn-based tactical combat system around the joy of having Iron Man, Dr. Strange, Blade, and more knock enemies around like toys they're trying to break – and that hasn’t gotten old in the roughly 75 hours of its surprisingly expansive RPG campaign. A lot of that time isn’t spent in battles, though, and while it’s certainly appealing to get up close and personal with this cast of more than a dozen popular and lesser-known Marvel heroes, it does tend to go a bit overboard with convincing Earth’s mightiest heroes to all be your BFFs.

title: Hogwarts Legacy Review - IGN
description: Like many, I’ve been waiting for a truly excellent Harry Potter game since I was in the third grade. In that time, we’ve gotten some respectable LEGO Potter games, an underwhelming EA Sports Quidditch game for some reason, and even suffered through the fevered nightmare that is Harry Potter Kinect. But none of these has come close to fulfilling that fantasy of receiving a Hogwarts admission letter that opens the door to a secret world. With Hogwarts Legacy, I’m happy to say that we finally got a Harry Potter game that captures some of that magic. Its open world map absolutely nails the vibe of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, it has spellcasting combat that’s stupefyingly good, the characters that inhabit it are charming and unforgettable, and it is positively brimming with countless diversions to soak up dozens of hours of your time. It may not be the most impressive technical achievement and it is certainly cursed with a lack of enemy variety, but none of Hogwarts Legacy’s issues can cast a Descendo charm on this triumphant visit to the Wizarding World.

title: Hivemapper is 1M kilometers closer to goal of beating Google Maps
description:
Hivemapper relied on ride-hail, delivery and truck drivers with dash cams to collect 1 million unique kms of fresh map data.

Hivemapper, the startup that puts dashcams on ride-hail and delivery vehicles to map the world, is getting a little closer to its goal of toppling the B2B mapping empire that Google has built.

With only 2% of the world’s roads mapped, Hivemapper is still very much the underdog in this fight. But Gabe Nelson, Hivemapper’s head of operations, reckons the startup is reaching an inflection point that will lead to exponential scale.

Hivemapper said Thursday it collected more than 1 million kilometers (about 620,000 miles) of unique street-level imagery. Compared to Google’s 60 million kilometers, that’s small potatoes. However, Hivemapper collected this data over the last three months. It took Google from 2007 to 2019 to collect 16.1 million kilometers of unique road data.

Now the startup aims to map 10 million unique road kilometers by early next year.

Hivemapper relies on individual contributors around the world to collect its street-view data, rather than spending millions of dollars putting dedicated mapping vehicles on the road. Its dashcams are equipped with a high-quality imager and precise GPS, and they go for $549. Mapping with dashcams, the company says, means its data is continuously being refreshed, whereas much of Google’s Street View imagery, particularly outside of urban centers, is over a decade old.
longFormSummary:
• The TechCrunch article covers Hivemapper, a startup that pays ride-hail, delivery, and truck drivers to mount dashcams on their vehicles in order to build a street-level mapping dataset that competes with Google Maps.
  • As of the March 2023 announcement, Hivemapper had collected over 1 million unique kilometers of imagery in about three months, using a network of more than 11,000 contributors across 418 regions.
  • By comparison, Google has mapped roughly 60 million kilometers total, taking from 2007 to 2019 to reach 16.1 million kilometers of unique road data.
  • Hivemapper's dashcams cost $549 and use GPS plus imaging hardware; the company argues its crowdsourced approach keeps imagery continuously refreshed compared to Google's Street View data, some of which is over a decade old in non-urban areas.
  • Drivers are compensated in a token called HONEY, from a fixed total supply of 10 billion, and fleet operators get dashboards to track earnings; the company offers higher rewards in targeted regions including South Korea, the Netherlands, Portugal, London, Paris, Madrid, and Tokyo to accelerate coverage.
  • With only about 2% of the world's roads mapped so far, Hivemapper's next stated goal is to reach 10 million unique kilometers by early the following year.

title: Resident Evil 4 Review  - IGN
description: In light of the high-quality remakes of Resident Evil 2 and 3 released in 2019 and 2020, it felt like a safe bet that Capcom would do an equally admirable job of rebuilding Resident Evil 4. Even so, when I hit the start button on this 2023 remake of the legendary 2005 action-horror game I wasn’t prepared for how forcefully it would knock my knees out from under me and suplex me headfirst into 16 hours of sustained tension and exhilaration. This fully revitalised campaign dramatically one-ups the original in almost every conceivable way. Its Spanish countryside setting is substantially more sinister, its pacing has been tightened to the point where hardly a single minute is wasted, and its controls have been modernised in order to allow its signature dynamic shooting mechanics to really shine. I’ve been waiting 18 years for a game to thrill me in the same way as Resident Evil 4; as it turns out, this whole time I’ve just been waiting for another Resident Evil 4.

title: Street Fighter 6 is scheduled to release on June 2, 2023 on PC, Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5
description:
The next evolution of the Street Fighter series is almost here, focusing heavily on single-player elements to ensure there’s plenty of content for every level of fighter. Street Fighter 5 was heavily criticized at launch for its lack of playable content outside of versus mode and while this satisfied most high-level players, casual players found there was very little to keep them entertained.
Capcom has taken its time developing Street Fighter 6 to ensure they don’t repeat the same mistakes again. It features a brand new single-player story mode which gives players a chance to explore Metro City as a custom fighter. Street Fighter 6 is shaping up to become one of the best fighting games and potentially one of the best PC games overall.
longFormSummary:
• Street Fighter 6 launched on June 2, 2023 for PC, Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5 (it is not on Xbox Game Pass).
  • Capcom built the game around a new single-player World Tour mode that lets players explore Metro City as a custom fighter, marking the series' first real narrative progression since Street Fighter III: Third Strike more than 20 years earlier -- a direct response to criticism that Street Fighter V launched with too little content for casual players.
  • The game introduces a Modern control type that simplifies special moves and combos to single-button inputs for newcomers, alongside a unified Drive gauge powering five techniques (Drive Impact, Drive Parry, Drive Reversal, Drive Rush, and Overdrive Arts) revived and reworked from earlier games in the series.
  • A social Battle Hub lets players interact via avatars, play arcade cabinets featuring Capcom classics like Street Fighter Alpha 2 and Final Fight, join tournaments through an Event Counter, and customize their avatar in a Body Shop.
  • The game supports full crossplay across PlayStation, Xbox, and PC, with an option to disable it.

title: San Francisco's Millennium Tower Fix Declared a Success
description: Engineers completed a $100M underpinning project meant to arrest the sinking and tilt of San Francisco's Millennium Tower.
longFormSummary:
• The 58-storey Millennium Tower had sunk more than a foot and tilted around 30 inches to the northwest since opening in 2009, largely because its foundation wasn't anchored to bedrock.
  • The fix drove 18 new concrete piles down to bedrock around the building's perimeter and gradually shifted a portion of the tower's load onto them.
  • Work on the piles began in late 2020 and the load-transfer process finished in mid-2023, after an earlier design was paused and reworked.

title: Insider Shares More On Tesla's Project Highland AKA Model 3 Refresh
description:
Several test prototypes have already been spotted with camouflaged front and rear ends, suggesting the Model 3 is in for some major visual updates. But Tesla's compact sedan will get more than that. According to a "trusted insider" who offered an exclusive insight to Not A Tesla App, the Project Highland will bring significant changes inside and out. 

Starting with the design, the report notes the headlights will have a different shape, which means the front bumper will be redesigned as well. It will be more aerodynamic and will now house a single camera in the center area of the lower grille, in similar fashion to the Cybertruck.

Out back, the refreshed Tesla Model 3 is also getting a redesigned bumper, although the changes will likely be purely for aesthetic reasons.

The source also said the side mirrors will be subtly updated and the Project Highland will be getting more cameras to take advantage of the new Hardware 4.0 Autopilot supercomputer. Three new cameras will reportedly be added to the Model 3: one in the center of the front bumper and two on the sides of the car.

title: Elon Musk announces timing for Tesla Cybertruck delivery event
description:
In a conference call following the release of the results, CEO Elon Musk made new comments announcing that Tesla plans to hold a “handover event,” which generally means the first deliveries of a new car, toward “the end of the third quarter.”

This would put the first Tesla Cybertruck deliveries around September 2023. It’s the most precise timing of Cybertruck deliveries that Tesla has released to date.

Based on the launch of Tesla’s most recent models, especially the Model Y, we should expect Tesla to only deliver a few Cybertrucks during the delivery event, likely only to Tesla insiders, and we can expect months between the event and the start of deliveries to customers.

Interestingly, Musk also said that Cybertruck reservation holders should expect to get an update on specs and pricing at that event at the end of Q3.

In previous comments, Musk indicated that the Cybertruck would be available in a new top-of-the-line variant with quad motors rather than the tri-motor powertrain originally announced.

  • Musk said reservation holders should expect an update on specs and pricing at that Q3 event, since the original 2019 pricing is expected to no longer apply.
  • He also indicated a new top-of-the-line quad-motor variant may be offered, replacing the tri-motor powertrain that had originally been announced.
  • Drawing on the pattern of past Tesla launches like the Model Y, the article cautions that such handover events usually involve only a handful of deliveries, largely to Tesla insiders, with broader customer deliveries following months later.

title: Panama Canal Wins Approval for Rio Indio Reservoir
description: Panama's Supreme Court overturned a 2006 law blocking new reservoirs, clearing the way for a dam on the Rio Indio meant to secure the Panama Canal's water supply against worsening droughts.
longFormSummary:
• Reduced rainfall driven by climate change has repeatedly forced the canal to limit daily ship transits, threatening a route that carries roughly 3% of global maritime trade and nearly half of US sea freight.
  • The Rio Indio plan, first devised in the 1990s, would dam the river to create a reservoir feeding Lake Gatun through an 8km tunnel, but a 2006 law had barred the canal authority from building reservoirs outside its existing watershed.
  • Panama's Supreme Court overturned that law in 2024, though the project still faces opposition from roughly 500 families whose homes lie in the area to be flooded.

title: Chicago's Century and Consumers Buildings Saved From Demolition
description: The US General Services Administration reversed course on a $52M congressional earmark to demolish two historic Chicago Loop skyscrapers, opting to reuse them instead after a sustained preservation campaign.
longFormSummary:
• The Century and Consumers Buildings, completed in the 1910s, were early examples of the steel-frame Chicago School of Architecture pioneered after the Great Chicago Fire.
  • Congress had earmarked $52M to demolish both towers plus a smaller building between them, citing security concerns for the neighbouring Dirksen Federal Courthouse.
  • A federally mandated environmental review found demolition would cause meaningful harm to the historic structures, prompting the GSA to seek adaptive-reuse proposals instead.
  • Both buildings went on to receive official Chicago Landmark status, closing out a preservation fight that had run for more than a decade.
address: 220 South State Street, Loop, Chicago, Illinois, United States

title: The Hawaii Mars Flying Boat Retires to a British Columbia Museum

longFormSummary:
• The Martin JRM Mars was the largest Allied flying boat of World War II, first flown in 1942, with seven aircraft built between 1945 and 1948.
  • Coulson Aviation of Port Alberni, British Columbia bought the last Mars aircraft in 2007 and flew "Hawaii Mars" and "Philippine Mars" as aerial firefighters until 2015.

  • The Mars could scoop water from nearby lakes and drop more than 25,000 litres per run on wildfires, making it the world’s largest operational water bomber.

title: Dresden's Carola Bridge Collapses Into the Elbe
description: A section of the 1971-built Carola Bridge in Dresden, Germany collapsed into the Elbe overnight with no warning, minutes after the last tram had crossed it.
longFormSummary:
• Deck C of the Carolabrücke, a tram, bike and pedestrian crossing built in 1971, fell into the Elbe in the early hours, just after a tram had passed over it, with no injuries reported.
  • The collapse blocked river shipping through central Dresden for months and became a widely cited symbol of Germany's ageing, under-maintained transport infrastructure.
  • Inspectors later found matching structural flaws in the bridge's other two decks, and the remaining structure was fully demolished through 2025.
  • The episode helped build political momentum behind Germany's subsequent €500BN infrastructure renewal fund, passed outside the country's normal debt-brake rules.

title: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam Inaugurated
description: Africa's largest hydroelectric plant at 5.15 GW, filled over five years amid a long dispute with Egypt and Sudan over Nile flows.
longFormSummary:
• The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam is a gravity dam on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia's Benishangul-Gumuz Region near the Sudanese border, built primarily to generate hydroelectric power.
  • With an installed capacity of 5.15 gigawatts across 13 turbines, it is Africa's largest hydroelectric plant and one of the twenty largest in the world, expected to produce about 15.76 TWh annually.
  • Ethiopia filled the dam's reservoir in five stages between 2020 and 2024, raising the water level from 540 meters in the first phase to its full 640-meter capacity by October 2024, with power generation beginning in February 2022 as successive turbines came online.
  • The filling and construction were the subject of a long-running dispute with downstream Egypt and Sudan, since Egypt draws roughly 90% of its water from the Nile and repeatedly warned of reduced water access, with negotiations stalling for years and Egypt at times threatening diplomatic and even military responses.
  • Construction was declared complete in late 2024, and the dam was formally inaugurated on September 9, 2025.

title: Grand Egyptian Museum Fully Open
description: Two decades and a billion dollars in the making, the largest archaeological museum in the world, holding the complete Tutankhamun collection.
longFormSummary:
• The Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza is the largest museum in the world dedicated to a single civilization, housing more than 100,000 ancient Egyptian artifacts spanning from the Predynastic Period through Roman Egypt within a 500,000-square-meter, triangular building.
  • The building was designed by Irish architects Róisín Heneghan and Shih-Fu Peng, sited about 2 kilometers from the Giza Pyramids and aligned so its walls frame views of the Great Pyramid and the Pyramid of Menkaure.
  • First announced in 1992, with its foundation stone laid in 2002 and construction beginning in earnest in 2005, the roughly $1.2 billion building was completed in 2023 after repeated delays from COVID-19 and regional security concerns.

title: Sagrada Família Tower of Jesus Christ Completed
description: Barcelona's basilica tops out its 172.5-metre central tower, making it the world's tallest church, timed for the centenary of Antoni Gaudí's death. Estimated date.
longFormSummary:
• The Sagrada Família is Antoni Gaudí's Catholic basilica in Barcelona's Eixample district, under construction since 1882 and consecrated as a minor basilica by Pope Benedict XVI in 2010.
  • Gaudí took over the design in 1883, blending Gothic and Art Nouveau styles with tree-like columns, hyperboloid surfaces, and three grand façades (Nativity, Passion, and Glory); when he died in 1926 the building was only 15-25% complete.
  • Construction was set back further when anarchists destroyed part of the structure and his original plans during the 1936 Spanish Civil War; work resumed in the 1950s and accelerated with computer-aided design, funded entirely by private donations and visitor entrance fees, with an annual construction budget of around €25 million.
  • The basilica surpassed Ulm Minster to become the world's tallest church at 162.91 meters in October 2025, and its central Tower of Jesus Christ reached its full designed height of 172.5 meters in February 2026.
  • Pope Leo XIV blessed and inaugurated the completed tower on June 10, 2026, timed to coincide with the centenary of Gaudí's death, though decorative elements and interior spires are expected to continue until around 2028-2032.

title: 235 East 42nd Street Column Buckling

title: Queensland Reverses Course, Commits to Rebuilding Paradise Dam Wall in Place
description: Queensland abandoned its plan for a new downstream dam in July 2026 and committed instead to rebuilding Paradise Dam's existing wall back to its original height.
longFormSummary:
• The dam's wall was lowered by 5.8 metres in 2020 after engineers found its roller-compacted concrete was degrading faster than expected.
  • A 2024 plan to abandon the existing wall and build a smaller replacement dam 70 metres downstream was later budgeted at roughly AU$4.4BN.
  • After the dam operator's own board chair called that downstream option disproportionate, Premier David Crisafulli rejected it and committed to restoring the original wall instead.
  • The government has allocated an initial AU$60M for geotechnical investigations and site preparation under the restored-wall approach.

title: Co-Owners Scrap the €800M Tour Montparnasse Overhaul
description: Ten years after Paris approved Nouvelle AOM's full glass-facade transformation of the Tour Montparnasse, the tower's co-owners voted to abandon that plan in favour of a smaller, cheaper intervention.
longFormSummary:
• Completed in 1973, the Tour Montparnasse is still the only skyscraper inside central Paris; the backlash to it led France to ban tall buildings in the city centre just four years later.
  • In 2017 Paris approved a Nouvelle AOM-designed renovation meant to strip the tower to its frame and wrap it in transparent glazing and sky gardens, with tenants vacating by March 2026 ahead of construction.
  • Discovered asbestos and rising costs pushed the budget from an original €624 million toward €800 million, and at a 21 July 2026 general assembly, co-owner LFPI refused further funding, killing the original design.
  • Asbestos removal and partial facade work are still going ahead from September 2026, while architects are now tasked with designing a cheaper version before the building permit lapses in November 2026.

title: Gordie Howe International Bridge Opens
description: A 853-metre cable-stayed span over the Detroit River, the longest in North America, carrying the busiest US-Canada trade corridor. Estimated date.
longFormSummary:
• The Gordie Howe International Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge connecting Detroit, Michigan to Windsor, Ontario across the Detroit River, named for the hockey legend, with twin 220-meter towers shaped to evoke a hockey stick mid-slapshot.
  • The 2.5 km structure has an 853-meter main span, the longest cable-stayed span in North America, supported by 216 cable stays, and carries six automotive lanes plus a pedestrian and bicycle path 46 meters above the water.
  • It was funded entirely by the Canadian federal government at a cost of roughly CA$6.4 billion.
  • It is intended to relieve the nearby Ambassador Bridge, which currently carries about a quarter of all US-Canada truck traffic, by giving Interstate 75 a direct, uninterrupted connection to Highway 401 without routing through city streets, supporting bilateral automotive trade that reached US$51 billion in 2023 and serving roughly 5,000 Canadian commuters who work in Detroit daily.
  • Construction ran from June 2018 to June 2026, with the bridge inaugurated on July 24, 2026 and opened to traffic on July 27, 2026, well behind its original 2024 target due to COVID-19 and other delays.
