title: Western Sydney International Airport Opens
description: Sydney's second international gateway at Badgerys Creek begins commercial flights, built with a 24-hour curfew-free runway. Estimated date.
longFormSummary:
• Western Sydney Airport (IATA: WSI) is a new international airport under construction about 44 km west of Sydney's CBD in Badgerys Creek and Luddenham, New South Wales, built to relieve pressure on the curfew-restricted Sydney (Kingsford Smith) Airport.
  • Its single 3.7 km runway is designed to handle large aircraft such as the Boeing 747 and Airbus A380, and unlike Sydney Airport it will operate 24 hours a day without a curfew; it is also Australia's first airport without an on-site control tower, instead using a remote digital tower with cameras feeding controllers 20 km away.
  • The integrated terminal has 14 gates and automated baggage handling, alongside a 75,000-square-metre cargo precinct designed to handle over 220,000 tonnes of freight a year.
  • Construction on Stage 1 began in September 2018, with the runway finished in January 2024 and the terminal completed in June 2025.
  • Cargo operations started on July 27, 2026, and passenger services are scheduled to begin October 25, 2026, with Jetstar's first domestic flight to the Gold Coast, followed a day later by Air New Zealand's international service to Auckland; Stage 1 is designed to handle up to 10 million passengers annually, with room to expand toward 82 million passengers via a second runway and larger terminals.

title: BepiColombo Enters Mercury Orbit
description: After seven years and nine planetary flybys, the joint ESA/JAXA mission separates into two orbiters to study Mercury. Scheduled date.
longFormSummary:
• BepiColombo is a joint ESA-JAXA mission to Mercury made up of two orbiters, ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mio (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter), designed to study the planet's magnetic field, magnetosphere, interior structure, and surface composition.
  • The spacecraft, with a combined mass of about 4,100 kg, launched October 20, 2018, on an Ariane 5 from French Guiana.
  • Its cruise phase included nine gravity-assist flybys: one of Earth (April 2020), two of Venus (October 2020 and August 2021), and six of Mercury itself (October 2021 through January 2025), at altitudes ranging from 37,626 km down to just 165 km.
  • Thruster problems discovered in September 2024 pushed Mercury orbit insertion back from an original December 2025 target; the Mercury Transfer Module separated on September 3, 2026, beginning the arrival phase, with orbit insertion now set for November 21, 2026.
  • After insertion, the two orbiters will separate into independent orbits, with Mio at a higher altitude (590 x 11,640 km) and MPO lower, and the pair will collaborate on roughly a year of scientific observations.

title: Thirty Meter Telescope Decision Deadline
description: A 30-metre segmented-mirror telescope stalled for a decade by opposition to building on Mauna Kea, with La Palma as the alternate site. Estimated date.
longFormSummary:
• The Thirty Meter Telescope is a proposed extremely large telescope with a 30-meter primary mirror made of 492 hexagonal segments, offering nine times the light-gathering power of the Keck Observatory and covering wavelengths from near-ultraviolet to mid-infrared with adaptive optics.
  • Its planned site atop Mauna Kea in Hawaii, considered the most sacred mountain in Hawaiian culture, has drawn sustained Native Hawaiian protests since 2014.
  • Hawaii's Supreme Court invalidated the original 2011 construction permit in December 2015 over procedural violations, a revised permit was approved in 2018, and blockades in 2014-2015 and a four-week standoff in July 2019 repeatedly halted construction, which has been stalled since 2015.
  • La Palma in Spain's Canary Islands was proposed as a backup site after the 2019 protests, though astronomers consider it scientifically inferior due to atmospheric water vapor interfering with mid-infrared observations, and a Spanish court revoked land concessions there in 2021 before the issue was resolved by 2023.
  • In June 2025, the U.S. National Science Foundation withdrew its support for the project in favor of the competing Giant Magellan Telescope, and while the international TMT consortium says it intends to proceed, the project's future funding remains highly uncertain.

title: HS2 London to Birmingham Opens

title: Halley's Comet Returns to Perihelion
description: The most famous comet swings back through the inner solar system on its 76-year orbit, having last appeared in 1986.
longFormSummary:
• Halley's Comet, officially designated 1P/Halley, is the only short-period comet consistently visible to the naked eye from Earth, a "dirty snowball" of ice and dust with a nucleus roughly 11 kilometers across.
  • It follows a highly elliptical, retrograde orbit lasting 74 to 79 years, swinging from a perihelion of just 0.59 astronomical units from the Sun out to an aphelion of 35 AU, nearly reaching Pluto's orbit.
  • Its appearances have been recorded since at least 240 BC in Chinese records, and its 1066 passage is depicted on the Bayeux Tapestry.
  • English astronomer Edmond Halley established its periodicity in 1705 by matching observations from 1531, 1607, and 1682, correctly predicting its return in 1758.
  • Having last appeared in February 1986, the comet is expected to return to the inner solar system around mid-2061, with its perihelion passage predicted for either July 28, 2061 or, under an alternate calculation accounting for gravitational perturbations, March 27, 2134.
dateConfidenceReasoning: No wording about the date found on en.wikipedia.org; treat it as unverified.
